definitions.gloss: a persimmon variety that is astringent when raw
definitions.explanation: A type of persimmon that tastes harshly astringent when eaten fresh. It becomes sweet only after the astringency is removed by drying or other treatment.

examples.japanese: この{柿|かき}は{渋柿|しぶがき}だ。
examples.english: This persimmon is an astringent one.

examples.japanese: {渋柿|しぶがき}をむいて{干|ほ}し{柿|がき}を{作|つく}る。
examples.english: We peel astringent persimmons to make dried persimmons.

examples.japanese: {渋柿|しぶがき}はそのまま{食|た}べると{渋|しぶ}くて、{渋抜|しぶぬ}きをしてから{食|た}べる。
examples.english: Astringent persimmons are too astringent to eat raw, so they are eaten after the astringency has been removed.

notes:
Composed of {渋|しぶ} (astringent) + {柿|かき} (persimmon). The astringency comes from tannins; it is removed ({渋抜|しぶぬ}き) by drying, or by treating with alcohol or warm water, which turns the fruit sweet.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {渋柿|しぶがき}の{渋抜|しぶぬ}き: removing astringency from persimmons
- {渋柿|しぶがき}を{干|ほ}す: to dry astringent persimmons

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {甘柿|あまがき}: sweet persimmon — a variety that is sweet and can be eaten fresh
- {干|ほ}し{柿|がき}: dried persimmon — made by drying astringent persimmons until sweet
